title: Sifted nerves, finite diagonals, and the geometric realization index
statement:
Use the universes, spaces and infinity categories of [def-coef-complete-algebroid] and the simplex category $\Delta$ of [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-set]. An infinity category $K$ is sifted when its colimit functor $\operatorname{Fun}(K,\mathcal S)\to\mathcal S$ on spaces preserves finite products. This is equivalent to $K$ being nonempty and its diagonal $K\to K\times K$ being final; final means that restriction preserves colimit cocones of every diagram admitting a colimit. Such $K$ is weakly contractible, meaning its localization at all arrows is equivalent to the one-point space. For each integer $n\geq0$, the finite diagonal $K\to K^n$ is final, including $n=0$ where $K^0$ is the terminal infinity category.

If $K=N(I)$ for a small ordinary category $I$, then $I$ is nonempty and connected and all its finite diagonal functors $I\to I^n$ are final in the ordinary sense: restriction along them preserves ordinary colimits. In particular, for ordinary cocomplete categories $\mathcal C_1,\ldots,\mathcal C_n,\mathcal E$, a functor $F:\prod_{a=1}^n\mathcal C_a\to\mathcal E$ preserving colimits separately, and diagrams $X_a:I\to\mathcal C_a$ for $1\leq a\leq n$, the canonical map
$$\operatorname{colim}_{i\in I}F(X_1(i),\ldots,X_n(i))\longrightarrow F(\operatorname{colim}_{i\in I}X_1(i),\ldots,\operatorname{colim}_{i\in I}X_n(i))$$
is an isomorphism. The same comparison is an equivalence when the categories are cocomplete infinity categories, the $X_a:N(I)\to\mathcal C_a$ are coherent diagrams, and $F$ preserves colimits separately. For $n=0$, the comparison says that the colimit of a constant diagram is its value. Finally $N(\Delta^{\mathrm{op}})$ is sifted, so the preceding assertions apply to geometric realization, namely colimit of a coherent simplicial diagram.

source.place: Higher Topos Theory, Definition 5.5.8.1, Warning 5.5.8.2, Lemma 5.5.8.4 and Propositions 5.5.8.6-7, printed pp. 506-507, and Lemma 5.5.8.11 (spaces). Finite diagonals follow by iteration; ordinary finality follows by taking components of coherent cocones. Online source read, not archived in literature/. No Stacks tag states this homotopy-coherent result.

proof.text:
We first derive separate product preservation in spaces from the existing transport interface. At the point, that interface identifies $\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal S}(U,V)$ with the Kan complex $\operatorname{Fun}(U,V)$, coherently in both variables; degreewise products therefore satisfy $\operatorname{Map}(T,X\times Y)=\operatorname{Map}(T,X)\times\operatorname{Map}(T,Y)$, and the point is terminal. The exponential identity of simplicial maps, obtained by rearranging factors in $T\times X\times Y\times\Delta^r$, gives $\operatorname{Map}(X\times Y,Z)\simeq\operatorname{Map}(Y,\operatorname{Fun}(X,Z))$; the universal-arrow theorem assembles this into the adjunction $X\times-\dashv\operatorname{Fun}(X,-)$ and its coherent-diagram formula. If $L=\operatorname{colim}_A D$, apply that formula and the cocone criterion to obtain
$$\operatorname{Map}(X\times L,Z)\simeq\operatorname{Map}(L,\operatorname{Fun}(X,Z))\simeq\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(A,\mathcal S)}(D,\Delta_A\operatorname{Fun}(X,Z))\simeq\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(A,\mathcal S)}(X\times D,\Delta_A Z).$$
Thus $X\times L$ with legs $\mathrm{id}_X\times\lambda_a$ is the colimit. Naturality is the stated coherent naturality of transport and universal arrows, and restriction of each formula along $\Delta^s\to\Delta^r$ commutes with factor rearrangement. Empty $A$ and empty $X$ are included.

source.place: Elementary universal-property calculation behind Lemma 5.5.2.3 and Remark 5.5.8.12; uses existing coherent universal-arrow and cocone interfaces.

proof.text:
For small simplicial sets $A,B$ and a quasicategory $\mathcal E$ with small colimits, the cocone criterion and the left-adjoint clause of the universal-arrow theorem supply $\operatorname{colim}_A\dashv\Delta_A$ and $\operatorname{colim}_B\dashv\Delta_B$, with their coherent-diagram mapping-space formulas. Curry $H:A\times B\to\mathcal E$ by rearranging the simplicial factors; for every $T\in\mathcal E$ these formulas give
$$\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal E}(\operatorname{colim}_A\operatorname{colim}_B H,T)\simeq\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(A,\mathcal E)}(\operatorname{colim}_B H,\Delta_A T)\simeq\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(A\times B,\mathcal E)}(H,\Delta_{A\times B}T).$$
The cocone criterion proves that the iterated colimit is the total colimit, with leg $H(a,b)\to\operatorname{colim}_B H(a,-)\to\operatorname{colim}_A\operatorname{colim}_B H$; exchanging $A,B$ proves the other order. Naturality, including higher simplices and all leg compatibilities, follows directly from the parameter and evaluation clauses of the cited universal-arrow statement. This argument includes empty shapes.

source.place: Elementary universal-property calculation behind Lemma 5.5.2.3 and Remark 5.5.8.12; uses existing coherent universal-arrow and cocone interfaces.

proof.text:
Using steps 1-2, record the independent-index calculation in spaces. For diagrams $X:A\to\mathcal S$ and $Y:B\to\mathcal S$, Fubini and separate colimit preservation of products give
$$\operatorname{colim}_{A\times B}(X(a)\times Y(b))\simeq(\operatorname{colim}_A X)\times(\operatorname{colim}_B Y).$$
At the $(a,b)$ leg this is the pair of the two colimit legs, by the explicit cocone-leg formulas in steps 1-2. For $a\in K$, put $h^a(k)=\operatorname{Map}_K(a,k)$. The identity functor of $K$ is final directly from its definition. Applying condition (4) of the cofinality criterion to that identity gives $\operatorname{colim}_K h^a\simeq *$. This is the coherent corepresentable-colimit calculation, without using any assertion about ordinary set-valued Yoneda.

source.place: Proof of Proposition 5.5.8.6 and Lemma 5.5.8.11; corepresentable colimit calculation from Kerodon 7.4.3.11(4) for the identity functor

proof.text: Assume the colimit functor on $K$-diagrams of spaces preserves finite products. If $K$ were empty, it would send the terminal diagram to the empty space, which is not terminal; thus $K$ has a vertex. For $a,b\in K$, binary product preservation and step 3 give $\operatorname{colim}_{k\in K}(h^a(k)\times h^b(k))\simeq *$. This product is the corepresentable functor $H_{K\times K}((a,b),-)$ restricted along $\delta$. Indeed $\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^1,K\times K)=\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^1,K)\times\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^1,K)$ degreewise, so the pullback along $\delta$ of the source-fixed arrow left fibration of $(a,b)$ is the fiber product over $K$ of the source-fixed arrow left fibrations of $a$ and of $b$. By the transport mapping-space formula, $\operatorname{Fun}_{/K}(E,E_1\times_KE_2)=\operatorname{Fun}_{/K}(E,E_1)\times\operatorname{Fun}_{/K}(E,E_2)$, so this fiber product classifies the product $h^a\times h^b$ in $\operatorname{Fun}(K,\mathcal S)$; on values it is the coordinatewise right-pinched formula $\operatorname{Map}_{K\times K}((a,b),(k,k))=\operatorname{Map}_K(a,k)\times\operatorname{Map}_K(b,k)$. Condition (4) of the cofinality criterion now applies to the diagonal $\delta:K\to K\times K$ and proves that $\delta$ is final. This uses only corepresentable tests, rather than assuming the equivalence being proved.

source.place: Definition 5.5.8.1 and converse to Lemma 5.5.8.11; Kerodon 7.4.3.11(4)

proof.text: Conversely suppose $K$ has a vertex and its diagonal is final. Put $B=\operatorname{colim}_K\operatorname{const}*$. Finality of the diagonal and step 3 identify the comparison $B\to\operatorname{colim}_{K\times K}\operatorname{const}*\simeq B\times B$ with the diagonal of $B$; it is an equivalence. The chosen vertex supplies a point $b_0$ of $B$. Since both projections are inverses to this diagonal, they are homotopic. Restricting that homotopy along $b\mapsto(b,b_0)$ gives $\mathrm{id}_B\simeq\operatorname{const}b_0$, so $B\simeq *$. For every space $T$, separate product preservation gives $\operatorname{colim}_K\operatorname{const}T\simeq B\times T\simeq T$, with the comparison to $T$ the projection. Condition (2) of the cofinality criterion implies that $K\to *$ is final; its comma category at the unique vertex is $K$ itself, so condition (3) proves weak contractibility. Finally the existing groupoid-localization theorem applied to the weak equivalence $K\to\Delta^0$ identifies $\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^0,\mathcal E)$ with all coherent functors $K\to\mathcal E$ inverting the arrows, for every $\mathcal E$. This is exactly localization of $K$ at all arrows, with value the one-point space.

source.place: Proof of Proposition 5.5.8.7, with the diagonal contraction written in spaces instead of homotopy groups

proof.text: For $X,Y:K\to\mathcal S$, diagonal finality followed by step 3 identifies $\operatorname{colim}_{k\in K}(X(k)\times Y(k))$ with $(\operatorname{colim}_K X)\times(\operatorname{colim}_K Y)$. The map is the binary product comparison because both its projections on each cocone leg are the original colimit legs. Step 5 gives the terminal-object comparison $\operatorname{colim}_K\operatorname{const}*\simeq *$. Induction on the number of factors, with terminal object as base and binary products as the induction step, proves preservation of every finite product. Together with step 4 this proves the claimed equivalence of the two definitions of siftedness.

Final functors compose: successively restricting a colimit cocone still gives a colimit cocone. They remain final after taking product with an identity: for $u:A\to B$ final, a space-valued diagram on $B\times L$ has the same colimit after restriction to $A\times L$, by applying finality at each fixed $l$ and then Fubini; condition (2) implies finality of $u\times\mathrm{id}_L$. The diagonal $\delta_1$ is the identity. If $\delta_n:K\to K^n$ is final with $n\geq1$, then
$$\delta_{n+1}=(\delta_n\times\mathrm{id}_K)\circ\delta_2$$
is final by these two facts. The base $n=0$ is $K\to *$, already proved final in step 5; this base is not inferred merely from nonemptiness. This proves all finite diagonal assertions.

source.place: Iteration of Definition 5.5.8.1; HTT Corollary 4.1.1.13, here derived using Fubini and the space test

proof.text: Let $K=N(I)$. More generally if $v:A\to B$ is an ordinary functor whose nerve is final, condition (3) says every ordinary $(b\downarrow v)$ has weakly contractible nerve, hence is nonempty and connected by finite zigzags of arrows (components of a nerve are exactly the equivalence classes of its vertices generated by its edges). Given a cocone $z_a:D(v(a))\to T$, define its extension at $b$ to be $z_aD(\beta)$ for any $(a,\beta:b\to v(a))$. A comma arrow leaves this composite unchanged by the cocone identity; connectedness makes it independent of the choice. For $g:b\to b'$, choose $(a,\beta':b'\to v(a))$ and use $(a,\beta'g)$ at $b$; then the extension satisfies $z_{b'}D(g)=z_b$. Choosing $(a,\mathrm{id})$ at $v(a)$ shows restriction recovers the original cocone, and extending a restricted cocone recovers it by its original naturality. These inverse extensions work for every vertex $T$ and commute with maps of vertices, so restriction preserves and reflects ordinary colimit cocones. Apply this to each $I\to I^n$, using $N(I^n)=N(I)^n$, to get ordinary finality. Taking $n=0$ gives that $I$ is nonempty and connected, including the required nullary assertion.

source.place: Warning 5.5.8.2; ordinary finality proved by explicit extension of cocones, not identified with homotopy finality

proof.text: For $n\geq1$ form the ordinary diagram $H:I^n\to\mathcal E$, $H(i_1,\ldots,i_n)=F(X_1(i_1),\ldots,X_n(i_n))$. Its colimit is the iterated colimit: a compatible family of maps from all $H(i_1,\ldots,i_n)$ to $T$ is equivalently a family compatible in one coordinate at a time, and applying each universal property gives the same maps to $T$. Fubini permits any order of iteration. Separate colimit preservation by $F$ therefore identifies this colimit with $F(\operatorname{colim}_I X_1,\ldots,\operatorname{colim}_I X_n)$. Step 8 identifies the colimit of $H$ with the colimit of $H\delta_n$. The composite comparison at each diagonal leg is $F$ applied to the original $X_a(i)\to\operatorname{colim}_I X_a$; hence it is the map displayed in the statement. For $n=0$, $F$ selects a single object of $\mathcal E$ and finality of $I\to *$ gives the identity constant cocone as its colimit.

source.place: Ordinary version of the independent-index calculation in HTT Proposition 5.5.8.6

proof.text: For the infinity-category comparison, form the coherent diagram $H:N(I)^n\to\mathcal E$, $H(i_1,\ldots,i_n)=F(X_1(i_1),\ldots,X_n(i_n))$, and apply step 2 repeatedly for $n\geq1$. At the $a$th iteration, preservation in the $a$th variable replaces $X_a(i_a)$ by $\operatorname{colim}X_a$, leaving the other arguments fixed. After $n$ iterations this computes its iterated colimit as $F(\operatorname{colim}X_1,\ldots,\operatorname{colim}X_n)$. Finality of $N(I)\to N(I)^n$ from step 7 identifies this colimit cocone with that of the diagonal restriction. The leg compatibility in Fubini identifies the resulting map with the canonical comparison, including all coherent compatibility data: at $(i_1,\ldots,i_n)$ its leg is $F(\lambda_{1,i_1},\ldots,\lambda_{n,i_n})$, and restricting the tuple to the diagonal gives $F(\lambda_{1,i},\ldots,\lambda_{n,i})$. For $n=1$ no interchange is needed; preservation by $F$ gives precisely this leg. For $n=0$, use finality $N(I)\to *$ on the diagram consisting of the object selected by $F$. Cocompleteness supplies all partial colimits; no filteredness, constructibility or model-category hypothesis is used.

It remains to check the geometric-realization index. The category $\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}$ is nonempty. For $([m],[n])$ in $(\Delta^{\mathrm{op}})^2$, its comma category under the diagonal is the opposite of the category $C$ of weakly increasing maps $\sigma:[r]\to P=[m]\times[n]$, where a morphism $\sigma\to\tau$ is a monotone $\theta$ with $\tau\theta=\sigma$. Let $Q$ be the poset of nonempty chains of $P$. Sending $\sigma$ to its image defines $R:C\to Q$, and increasing enumeration defines $J:Q\to C$. Then $RJ=\mathrm{id}_Q$ and the quotient map onto the image gives a natural transformation $\mathrm{id}_C\to JR$: for $\theta$ as above, both composites send an index $t$ to the position of $\sigma(t)$ in the image of $\tau$. Let $p_0=(0,0)$ and $T(q)=q\cup\{p_0\}$. This is a chain since $p_0$ is the least element of $P$; inclusions give natural transformations $\mathrm{id}_Q\to T\leftarrow\operatorname{const}\{p_0\}$. The cited nerve-homotopy theorem makes these transformations a contraction of $NQ$, hence of $NC$. On opposite categories the transformations are $\mathrm{id}_{C^{\mathrm{op}}}\leftarrow J^{\mathrm{op}}R^{\mathrm{op}}$ and $\mathrm{id}_{Q^{\mathrm{op}}}\leftarrow T^{\mathrm{op}}\to\operatorname{const}\{p_0\}$, with $R^{\mathrm{op}}J^{\mathrm{op}}=\mathrm{id}_{Q^{\mathrm{op}}}$. The cited nerve-homotopy theorem contracts $N(C^{\mathrm{op}})$ through these displayed zigzags. The comma criterion proves finality of the diagonal of $N(\Delta^{\mathrm{op}})$. Steps 5-6 give siftedness, and steps 7-10 give every comparison for coherent simplicial diagrams, whose colimit is precisely the geometric realization in the statement.
